source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project (IFAD-funded) - "Climate Resilient Banana Growing Technique" (ផលិតកម្មដំណាំចេកដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ), November 2018
text:
Banana aphid is flagged as a high-priority pest not primarily for its own feeding damage but because it transmits Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV), an incurable viral disease that stunts the plant and bunches the leaves at the top of a narrow, non-fruiting stem. Because there is no cure, prevention is critical: controlling aphid populations with a registered insecticide and immediately removing and destroying any plant showing bunchy-top symptoms before the aphids on it can spread the virus further.

Farmers are also advised to source planting material only from clumps known to be free of bunchy top, since planting an already-infected sucker introduces the disease into a new field regardless of how well aphids are later controlled there.
